articleTitle: Insight: Leadership
abstract: Trying to work out what to do with your leadership day? Try random acts of authenticity, writes Jon G Hall CITP FBCS.

articleTitle: Insight: Futurology
abstract: There's a great joke in Douglas Adams’ The Restaurant at the End of the Universe… writes Matt Lucas FBCS, IBM customer success manager.

articleTitle: Is Time Up for TikTok?
abstract: It may be hard for you to believe that TikTok has only been around for less than four years, writes Jon Belcher, Specialist Data Protection and Information Governance Lawyer at Excello Law.

articleTitle: Architecting an Equal Future
abstract: Why is the number of women who occupy some of the most senior technical roles in our profession so small? Gillian Arnold FBCS, MD at Tectre, explores the issue.

articleTitle: How to be an IT Consultant
abstract: Being great in your chosen IT speciality isn't enough to be an IT consultant - it takes a lot more. Simon Wallace explores the range of skills you’ll need to develop if you plan on becoming an IT consultant.

articleTitle: How Chaos Theory is Changing Management Tech
abstract: As technology infrastructures are becoming more dynamical and business critical, so they are susceptible to chaos theory, writes Freelance Consultant Paul Taylor MBCS.

articleTitle: Insight: Leadership
abstract: What makes a good leader? By inviting us to play a game, Jon G Hall FBCS CITP explores an apparent gulf between our conscious and unconscious views about leadership.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Predictions 2021
abstract: Looking back on 2020, it is clear COVID-19 redefined the term ‘digital resilience’, writes Greg Day, VP and CSO EMEA of California-based Palo Alto Networks.

articleTitle: Insight: Business Analysis
abstract: We are facing a point of major divergence in the tech industry, writes Business Analysis Leader, Christina Lovelock MBCS.

articleTitle: Insight: Cybersecurity
abstract: Deepthi Ratnayake MBCS, Senior Lecturer in Computer Science, explains the Colonial Pipeline attack that revolutionised ransomware landscape.

articleTitle: The Lovelace Medal 2020
abstract: The BCS Lovelace Medal is an award for making significant contributions to the advancement of information systems. Martin Cooper MBCS meets the recipients.

articleTitle: Virtual Learning? It's Here to Stay!
abstract: Classroom‐based training has been a long‐established model for getting people together in a room with a trainer, writes John Young MBCS, Principal Trainer at TSG Training.

articleTitle: Making Workshops Work… Despite Complications
abstract: Workshops are a great way to collaborate with others, or at least they can be when things run smoothly, writes Penny Pullan MBCS.

articleTitle: Why is it Governance so Important?
abstract: Organisations need to implement suitable governance to ensure technology platforms are suitably controlled and managed, argues freelance consultant, Paul Taylor MBCS.

articleTitle: Beyond NFTs: A Possible Future for Digital Art
abstract: The Computer Arts Society, founded in 1969 as a BCS Special Interest Group and still going strong in its 51st year, has seen the ebb and flow of interest in various digital artforms, writes Dr Nick Lambert, Chair of the BCS Computer Arts Society SG.

articleTitle: Covid-19 and Digital Education: a Catalyst For Change?
abstract: While education still faces huge challenges, including the rapid shift to online learning, teaching and assessment, there may be some light at the end of the tunnel, writes Tom Crick MBE FBCS, Professor of Digital Education & Policy at Swansea University.

articleTitle: Using AI To Increase Project Management Maturity
abstract: Every company has goals. Part of running a business is knowing how to reach those goals in an effcient way, writes Lloyd Skinner, Chief Executive Offcer at Greyfly. Having dedicated project management in place isn't enough — it needs maturity.

articleTitle: Blockchain: The New Art House
abstract: NFTs (Non‐fungible tokens) have been thrust into the spotlight as companies, people and artists seek to monetise creations, from artworks to tweets. Philippe Gellman, co‐founder and CEO of Arteïa, talks to Johanna Hamilton about his creation of ‘the first Digital Catalogue Raisonné supported by blockchain’ and how cutting‐edge tech is changing the art world.

articleTitle: How Keyloggers Work and How To Defeat Them
abstract: Homeworking policies, necessary to curtail COVID-19, have also had the effect of exposing smaller enterprises to a level of sophisticated cyber-attack ordinarily reserved for large multi-nationals, writes Dave Waterson, CEO of SentryBay.

articleTitle: How Open Banking is Democratising Finance
abstract: Open banking is fuelling a fintech revolution and fostering a wave of apps which give customers more control of their money and insight into their finances. Martin Cooper MBCS interviews Constanza Castro Feijóo, Stakeholder Engagement Manager at the Open Banking Implementation Entity.

articleTitle: Diversity Report 2021: Slow Progress is Some Progress
abstract: BCS has produced four reports analysing the ONS Labour Force survey, looking at diversity issues in the IT space. For IT, the picture is mixed but with some encouraging trends. From an employer point of view, it is perhaps a tale of opportunities missed, but with implied potential. Brian Runciman MBCS writes.

articleTitle: IT Leaders Report: Cloud, Security & Soft Skills Come Into Their Own
abstract: Each January BCS produce a report informed by IT leaders. This year it was also the basis of the inaugural IT Leaders Forum event — ‘The Adaptive CIO’. Brian Runciman MBCS looks at some of the takeaways on concerns, priorities and skills gaps.

articleTitle: Lovelace Colloquium 2021
abstract: The 14th BCS Women Lovelace Colloquium for undergraduate and MSc women in computing was hosted by the University of Lancaster and was held online. Dr Safia Barikzai, Associate Professor at London South Bank University, describes the day.

articleTitle: The Most Influential Woman in Tech
abstract: Anne-Marie Imafidon MBE is Computer Weekly's most influential woman in tech 2020. She talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about awards, equality and why sometimes it's great to have compliments about your laptop and shoes.

articleTitle: Becoming a UX Pro
abstract: User experience (UX) is a rapidly growing specialism, essential to the design of modern technology. Vanessa Burgar DipHE MSc QTS CITP discusses what knowledge is needed for successful practice and considers how can we provide education for aspiring UX professionals that is fit-for-purpose and strengthens professional identity.

articleTitle: The Big Interview: How Money Laundering Works
abstract: How and why do cyber criminals hide their money's source? Dr Dionysios Demetis, Senior Lecturer in Management Systems at Hull University, explains.

articleTitle: How Microsoft Teams is Evolving
abstract: When the pandemic caused chaos across our working lives, Microsoft Teams, along with other collaboration tools, helped to keep the UK working. Nick Hedderman, Director, Modern Work & Security Business Group, Microsoft UK, spoke to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about this new normal.

articleTitle: The Roger Needham Award 2020
abstract: Professor Jade Alglave has won the BCS Roger Needham Award, sponsored by Microsoft Research Cambridge. The award has been made in recognition of her fundamental work in one of the more diffcult areas of computer science: concurrency. Martin Cooper MBCS reports.

articleTitle: The Big Interview: Language and Cybersecurity
abstract: Paul Vlissidis MBCS, Technical Director at NCC Group and author of How To Survive The Internet, tells Martin Cooper MBCS why the language cybersecurity uses might be hampering the industry's attempts to keep people and organisations safe.

articleTitle: Agile Sourcing: Find the Right Technology Partner Faster
abstract: If going out to tender fills you with dread, you’re not alone — suppliers feel the same. David Brook, IT Sourcing Specialist at Turnstone Services talks tenders and agile sourcing.

articleTitle: BCS Virtual Festival of Digital Skills
abstract: BCS successfully delivers virtual conference with the theme of nurturing digital skills to aid economic recovery post-COVID. Claire Penketh reports.

articleTitle: The Shape of Cloud Security in The WFH ERA
abstract: It's been a year since the first lockdown came into effect in the UK and brought with it the shift to working remotely, writes Danny Phillips, EMEA VP, Sales Engineering at Zscaler.

articleTitle: Integration of Formal Proof into Unified Assurance Cases - With Isabelle/SACM
abstract: The paper, by Simon Foster, Yakoub Nemouchi, Mario Gleirscher, Ran Wei and Tim Kelly, published in The Formal Aspects of Computing—Applicable Formal Methods (June 2021), explores the introduction of Isabelle/SACM into formal methods of assurance.

articleTitle: BCS Insights 2021
abstract: How a diverse and inclusive IT industry can help find solutions to the world's biggest problems, including the climate crisis, political oppression and existential threats to the internet's fabric. BCS Insights 2021 explores how we can all help make IT good for society.

articleTitle: Visualising Business Analysis
abstract: Visual thinking opens up new possibilities that can take your business analysis practices to the next level, writes Grant Wright, Principal Consultant at Scarlett Solutions and co-founder of The Visual Jam.

articleTitle: Designing a Chip That's Good For You
abstract: Carolyn Herzog, EVP and General Counsel at ARM talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about AI, diversity, inclusivity and the importance of matching the algorithm to the community.

articleTitle: The Future of Battery Tech
abstract: Dr. Soly Mathew Biju MBCS CITP and Alex Mathew explain common problems with lithium-ion batteries and explore technologies that could revolutionise power in everything — from cars to mobile phones.

articleTitle: How to Build a Strong it Talent Pipeline
abstract: When it comes to building an IT talent pipeline, Claire Dudley from QA says culture, engagement, and continuous learning are all important considerations.

articleTitle: The Illegal Economy and Crime as a Service
abstract: With the significant advances of technology over many years, not only have law‐abiding citizens, organisations and governments leveraged this to their advantage to grow and prosper, so too have criminals, writes David Fairman, CSO APAC at Netskope.

articleTitle: How Covid-19 Changed The Future
abstract: Naveen Madhavan PhD MBCS, Senior Product Specialist (Pathology) at the NHS Wales Informatics Service, assesses how COVID-19 has changed our perceptions of the workplace and explores the likely lasting influence for the virus on digital transformation.

articleTitle: When Computers Changed Banking
abstract: The story of a rivalry, drive‐in‐banking, a computer called Pegasus and a team with great vision. Martin Cooper MBCS explores the history of Martins Bank and its desire to be first at computers.

articleTitle: Introducing John Higgins
abstract: From the AGM in March, BCS has a new President. Brian Runciman MBCS speaks to John Higgins against a backdrop of a year when we hope some of the worst effects of COVID-19 will be starting to recede, and new priorities start emerging.

articleTitle: How Collaboration Can Address Digital Poverty
abstract: Being digitally excluded has a huge impact on everyday aspects of life, from lack of access to significant social improvements, to health and social care, write Dave Donaghy CITP CEng FRSA MBCS and Tom Crick MBE CEng FLSW FBCS.

articleTitle: BCS Impact Report: Autumn 2021
abstract: Following the abhorrent online racist abuse of England footballers after the Euro 2020 final, BCS was invited to comment by a range of international media, thanks to our recent members’ survey<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> on the topic, which provided an evidence base. Claire Penketh reports.

articleTitle: BCS Partner: Outsource.Dev - How to Optimise Teams When Outsourcing
abstract: Ideas for team building and organisational structures for software development projects involving internal staff and outsourced developers, from Greg Billington MBCS, CEO and Founder of outsource.dev.

articleTitle: EU Roadmap to Cleaner, Greener Data Centres
abstract: While our exit from the European Union is very much in the news, our shared purpose and collaboration with our neighbours isn't so widely celebrated. John Booth MBCS, Vice Chair of the Green IT SG and Managing Director of Carbon3IT, looks at energy hungry data centres and explains how (and why) the green tide is turning.

articleTitle: Reimagining The Internet With Edge Computing
abstract: Blesson Varghese, Associate Professor in computer science at Queen's University Belfast and Flavio Bonomi, Founder of Nebbiolo Technologies and Board Technology Adviser for LYNX, explore how edge computing could foster a more ethical and fairer internet.

articleTitle: IT's Biggest Risk: Social Engineering
abstract: It's not hackers but ‘nice people’ who unwittingly hand over the keys to the digital kingdom. Tony Sales, co‐founder of We Fight Fraud talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about his career and social engineering.

articleTitle: Tom Ilube: Defining Leadership, Culture and Strategy
abstract: Tom Ilube CBE FBCS sets a leadership example in an industry where it pays to take smart risks. In this interview with Blair Melsom MBCS, he talks about work, culture and rolling the dice.

articleTitle: How the Microbiome Can Help Avert a Climate Crisis
abstract: Advanced data management is starting to crack the hidden world mother nature has created around us. Anthony Finbow, Chief Executive Officer at Eagle Genomics ‐ a pioneer in applying network science to biology ‐ discusses how.

articleTitle: BCS Impact Report
abstract: As the third national lockdown throws the digital divide into sharper focus, BCS continues to speak boldly on issues from home-schooling to our analysis of the loss of police database records. Claire Penketh reports.

articleTitle: How on Earth Can You Help The World?
abstract: There is a shortage of skilled IT professionals and the need will increase hugely in the future, writes Dalim Basu FBCS, Chairman of BCS London Central and North London.

articleTitle: Data First Strategy for AI in Project Management Success
abstract: There are many benefits of using AI in your project management strategies, writes Lloyd Skinner, CEO of Greyfly. However, to really excel, there's one key thing to focus on: data.

articleTitle: IT System Management: A Service Provider Perspective
abstract: The adoption of digitisation has transformed organisations to become entirely reliant on information systems to function, writes Naveen Madhavan PhD MBCS, Senior Product Specialist (pathology) at Digital Health and Care Wales.

articleTitle: 10 Things You Need to Know About Data in 2021
abstract: Vanessa Barnett, Technology and Data Partner at Keystone Law, scans the data regulation horizon to warn of what's to come in the year ahead.

articleTitle: Insight: Business Analysis
abstract: Christina Lovelock MBCS explores the derivation of the word ‘analysis’ and explains how the word's true meanings can help us all become better analysts ourselves.

articleTitle: Defining Digital Capital and Digital Poverty
abstract: Dave Donaghy MBCS FRSA CITP CEng, Lead Engineer at Hewlett Packard Enterprise and BCS Council Member, explores how common language may help us to unify our approaches to problems in digital poverty.

articleTitle: From Gold Coins to Cryptocurrencies: A History of Money In 10 Minutes
abstract: The BCS Financial Services Specialist Group compresses over 2,000 years of history and explains how we moved from using gold coins to being on the brink of governments issuing their own central bank digital currencies.

articleTitle: How Do You Manage an Invisible Workforce?
abstract: A recent BCS LinkedIn poll revealed that mental health was at the top of managers’ list of WFH concerns. As author and troubleshooter Carole Osterweil explains, mental health is something you ignore at your peril!

articleTitle: AI and US: Engineering a Healthy Relationship
abstract: Jyoti Choudrie FBCS, Professor of Information Systems at the University of Hertfordshire, talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about COVID-19, sanity checking with seniors, robotics and how AI is shaping our world.

articleTitle: The Power of Data: Fixing Banking and the Climate
abstract: Ed Evans FBCS has been following developments in data and energy. He details a presentation given to the Data Management Specialist Group by Gavin Starks, CEO of Icebreaker One and one of the architects of open banking and open energy.

articleTitle: Blockchain: A Data Metamorphosis?
abstract: Do you believe the hype? Anthony Day, Blockchain Partner for IBM UK & Ireland, talks to Johanna Hamilton AMBCS about whether blockchain is a transformative tool or just a new way to do something we were already doing.

articleTitle: Are Central Bank Digital Currencies the Future of Cash?
abstract: William Lovell, Head of Future Technologies at the Bank of England, explores how central bank digital currencies might change money, the problems of a cashless society and how he's keeping bar staff guessing.

articleTitle: Redefining The Notion Of weakness In GR(1) Formulae
abstract: The paper ‘A Weakness Measure for GR(1) Formulae’, by Davide G. Cavezza, Dalal Alrajeh and András György, published in Formal Aspects of Computing, in November 2020, explores a new measure for assessing the weakness of GR(1) conjunctions quantitatively.
